issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int)' on SealSaloon, but the reference solution implements a static method named 'receiveDelivery(String, int, int)'. This name/signature mismatch (method identifier) is a structural inconsistency: students following the specification will implement or expect 'acceptSupplyDelivery', while the provided solution uses a different method name, which can confuse students and break tests that expect the specified name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution's 'receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' method to 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' (keeping it static and preserving its behavior), or update the problem statement and tests to expect 'receiveDelivery' instead.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the provided Main example) refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) for adding deliveries to the shared stock, but the solution implements this functionality under a different identifier receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This naming divergence (acceptSupplyDelivery vs receiveDelivery) refers to the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) and creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template will look for acceptSupplyDelivery, while the solution exposes receiveDelivery, causing confusion about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the delivery-accepting method across all artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery (keeping the same signature: static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)), or alternatively update the problem statement and template Main example to refer to receiveDelivery. Preferably implement acceptSupplyDelivery in the solution (optionally delegating to receiveDelivery) to match the exercise text and template.
